nasa-iss047e022280.caption: ISS047e022280 (03/26/2016) --- This interesting Earth observation image from the International Space Station seems an abstract painting but is really the outskirts of the Namib Desert in southwest Africa. One of the oldest and largest deserts in the world, the Namib stretches inland from the Atlantic Ocean, covering large swathes of Namibia and parts of Angola and South Africa. This arid hotspot surprisingly supports a diverse number of plants and animals, some of which are found nowhere else in the world.

commons-84344084.caption: Worm Bay at Port Campbell National Park, Peterborough, Victoria, AustraliaPort Campbell National Park is located on the south coast of Victoria along the Great Ocean Road and protects a spectacular coastal landscape of limestone, cliffs, caves, and natural bridges.Its geological formation dates back millions of years: over thousands of years, layers of limestone and shells formed caves, gateways, and towers, which were repeatedly eroded by the Southern Ocean. The coast also served as a habitat for indigenous groups in the region, including the Wergaia and Eastern Maar communities. From the 1950s/60s onwards, the area was designated a protected area to preserve its exceptional geology, wildlife, and flora and to manage visitor flows in a sensible manner.Special features include the famous limestone cliffs, narrow passages, natural bridges, and steep cliffs; highlights such as the Twelve Apostles, Loch Ard Gorge, and other coastal formations attract many visitors each year. The sea is home to seals, seabirds, and rich marine fauna, while the rocky shores also support maritime flora. Hiking trails, lookout points, and boat tours offer insights into geology, geomorphology, and coastal protection—a harmonious combination of natural wonders and historical perspective.

commons-169439444.caption: General Context: Infrared photograph taken at Ilha do Cardoso State Park, documenting the flooding of mangrove areas due to sea-level rise. Because of the infrared technique, the colours are unnatural. The composition is minimalist, divided almost exactly in half between the sky and the water. Foreground (Bottom half of the image): Occupies the entire lower half of the photo. It consists of a flat, smooth, and reflective surface of very shallow water over sand. The colour of this area is a uniform salmon-pink or light orange shade. On the left side, there is the elongated, inverted reflection of a tree, pointing towards the bottom edge of the image. Middle Ground (The Centre and Horizon Line):A straight, horizontal line divides the image in half. On the left side, off-centre, a single dead tree trunk rises directly from the water. The tree is leafless, its colour is reddish-brown, and its upper branches form a 'Y' shape. Along the entire horizon line, separating the water from the sky, there is a narrow, white, blurred band, resembling distant breaking waves or low mist. Background (Top half of the image): Occupies the upper half. It is composed entirely of the sky. The colour is a solid, continuous teal (cyan-blue), which slightly darkens at the top corners. There are small, thin white cloud formations concentrated just above the horizon line, and a solitary, wispy cloud in the upper right corner.

commons-121140288.caption: Lower Bankhead, Bankhead, Banff National Park, Alberta, CanadaBanff National Park in the Canadian province of Alberta was founded in 1885 and is Canada’s oldest national park. Its creation dates back to the discovery of hot springs on Sulphur Mountain, after which the area was placed under protection. Today, the park covers around 6,600 square kilometers in the Canadian Rocky Mountains and is part of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site “Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks”.The landscape is characterized by rugged peaks, glaciers, turquoise lakes such as Lake Louise, and dense coniferous forests. The park provides habitat for grizzly bears, wapiti, moose, and bighorn sheep. In addition to protecting the unique mountain environment, Banff is an important destination for hikers, skiers, and nature enthusiasts from all over the world.

commons-121140290.caption: Lower Bankhead, Bankhead, Banff National Park, Alberta, CanadaBanff National Park in the Canadian province of Alberta was founded in 1885 and is Canada’s oldest national park. Its creation dates back to the discovery of hot springs on Sulphur Mountain, after which the area was placed under protection. Today, the park covers around 6,600 square kilometers in the Canadian Rocky Mountains and is part of the UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site “Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks”.The landscape is characterized by rugged peaks, glaciers, turquoise lakes such as Lake Louise, and dense coniferous forests. The park provides habitat for grizzly bears, wapiti, moose, and bighorn sheep. In addition to protecting the unique mountain environment, Banff is an important destination for hikers, skiers, and nature enthusiasts from all over the world.

Dune 45 is composed of iron-rich quartz sand, whose deepening red tones result from the gradual oxidation of iron over millions of years. The sand grains originated from sediments carried by the Orange River into the Atlantic Ocean and transported northward by coastal currents before being blown inland by strong south-westerly winds. The Namib Desert itself is considered one of the oldest deserts on Earth—at least 5 million years old, and possibly up to 55–80 million years in its broader geological history. The dune fields around Sossusvlei, including Dune 45, are thought to have formed in their present configuration over the last 2–3 million years, shaped continually by wind-driven (aeolian) processes. Although the dune’s crest and slipface shift subtly over time, its overall structure remains relatively stable due to the region’s hyper-arid climate.

commons-118291276.caption: One of pictures of the exterior and interior, some during a time of restoration. There is a hall before entering the prayer room from which one can enter the mausoleum of Battal Gazi. The masjid was first built during the reign of Kılıç Aslanoğlu Sultan Keyhüsre in H.604 (1207 A.D.) and was renovated by Seyyid Güzelce Hüseyin in 1512. The jamb and lintel of the masjid door were black marble. The square planned sanctuary is covered with a large dome. The transition to the dome is provided by pendants. Mihrab is a semicircular niche. Origin found during repair. The original floor covering, preserved as it was, was unearthed. The pavilion is partially pyramid-conical minbar, made of monolithic stone.

commons-118291276.museumExcerpt: One of pictures of the exterior and interior, some during a time of restoration. There is a hall before entering the prayer room from which one can enter the mausoleum of Battal Gazi. The masjid was first built during the reign of Kılıç Aslanoğlu Sultan Keyhüsre in H.604 (1207 A.D.) and was renovated by Seyyid Güzelce Hüseyin in 1512. The jamb and lintel of the masjid door were black marble. The square planned sanctuary is covered with a large dome. The transition to the dome is provided by pendants. Mihrab is a semicircular niche. Origin found during repair. The original floor covering, preserved as it was, was unearthed. The pavilion is partially pyramid-conical minbar, made of monolithic stone.
